criteria.text: test_rejects_body_over_limit_without_content_length: a chunked body exceeding max_body_size gets a plain-text 413 'Content Too Large'.

test_multipart_upload_counts_overhead: multipart upload whose raw body (with boundaries) exceeds the limit is rejected with 413 even if file data alone is under the limit; streaming bodies are counted per chunk.
test_content_length_failfast: a declared Content-Length over the limit gets 413 before receive is called, even if the endpoint never reads the body.
test_understated_content_length_and_exact_limit: an understated Content-Length does not bypass the limit; a body exactly at the limit is accepted.
test_no_double_response: when the limit is crossed after the app started its response, the middleware sends no second response and receive raises HTTPException(413).
test_scope_key_set_and_restored: scope['starlette.max_body_size'] equals the limit inside the app and the previous value (or absence) is restored afterwards, including after errors.
test_max_body_size_kwarg: Starlette, Router, Mount and Route accept max_body_size and enforce it; default None leaves requests unlimited.

test_inner_limit_overrides_outer: an inner Route/Mount/Router limit can raise or lower the Starlette-level limit; application middleware that reads the body is subject to the application-level limit; Content-Length fail-fast applies when the endpoint never reads the body.

test_multipart_closes_tempfiles_on_interrupt: temp files created during multipart parsing are closed when parsing is interrupted by any exception, including HTTPException(413) raised from the stream mid-parse.
Middleware is pure ASGI, exports MAX_BODY_SIZE_SCOPE_KEY, and nothing new is exported from starlette/__init__ or the package root.
The existing test suite remains green.

intents.rationale: No body_limit module exists; create it.
Content-Length fail-fast plus counted-bytes enforcement must be implemented in the new middleware.
Middleware must track response start and raise HTTPException(413) from receive without sending a second response.
Scope key constant and set/restore logic are new.
Starlette, Router, Mount and Route have no max_body_size keyword.
Application limit goes into build_middleware_stack before routing; Route/Mount/Router wrap their app with the middleware so inner limits override after routing.
Only MultiPartException and OSError currently trigger closing temp files; must cover any interruption.
New tests are required in several test files.

summary: Add a pure ASGI RequestBodyLimitMiddleware module, fix multipart temp-file cleanup on any interruption, then wire a max_body_size kwarg into Starlette, Router, Mount and Route with outer-to-inner override via the scope key. Three tasks; the middleware and the formparsers fix are independent, and wiring depends on the middleware.

tasks.summary: Create RequestBodyLimitMiddleware and MAX_BODY_SIZE_SCOPE_KEY in starlette/middleware/body_limit.py with tests. Wrap receive to count bytes; Content-Length fail-fast; track response start to avoid a double response; raise HTTPException(413) from receive; set/restore the scope key.
In MultiPartParser.parse, close temp files on any exception (except BaseException) rather than only MultiPartException/OSError, then re-raise; add a test.

Add max_body_size: int | None = None to Starlette (inserted in build_middleware_stack after ServerErrorMiddleware and before user middleware), Router (wraps its routing app), Mount and Route (wrap self.app); None adds nothing. Inner limits override outer via the scope key. Add tests.
